topics.title: Present simple and continuous

topics.title: Present perfect simple and continuous

topics.title: Narrative tenses
topics.brief: Past simple, past continuous, past perfect simple and continuous together in a story; sequencing; when/while/as; by the time.

topics.title: used to, would, be used to, get used to
topics.brief: Past habits and states vs present habits; be/get used to + -ing; would only for repeated actions.

topics.title: Future forms
topics.brief: will/going to/present continuous/present simple; future continuous and future perfect; be about to, be likely to; time clauses (when/as soon as + present).

topics.title: Obligation, permission and advice
topics.brief: must/have to/should/ought to/needn't/don't have to/mustn't; be allowed to; had better; past forms (had to, should have).

topics.title: Speculation and deduction
topics.brief: must/might/may/could/can't for present and past (+ have + participle); degrees of certainty; continuous forms (must be joking).

topics.title: Conditionals: zero to third
topics.brief: The four types with their meanings; unless/as long as/provided that/in case/even if; were in the second conditional; alternatives to will in results.

topics.title: Mixed conditionals
topics.brief: Past cause with present result and present state with past result.

topics.title: wish, if only, would rather, it's time
topics.brief: wish/if only + past, past perfect and would; would rather + past; it's (high) time + past; as if/as though.

topics.title: The passive in all tenses
topics.brief: Forms across tenses and with modals; by + agent; verbs with two objects; it is said that / he is said to; when to prefer the passive.

topics.title: Causative: have/get something done
topics.brief: have/get + object + participle in all tenses; get sb to do; have sb do; make/let/allow; have something happen to you.

topics.title: Reported speech
topics.brief: Tense, pronoun, time and place shifts; reported questions (if/whether, word order); commands and requests; when the tense does not change.

topics.title: Reporting verbs and their patterns
topics.brief: suggest/recommend + -ing; deny/admit + -ing; accuse sb of; insist on; warn/advise/persuade sb (not) to; agree/offer/refuse + to; apologise for.

topics.title: Relative clauses
topics.brief: Defining vs non-defining (commas, that, omission); whose/where/when/why; which referring to a whole clause; prepositions in relative clauses; reduced relatives (-ing/-ed).

topics.title: Verb patterns: gerund and infinitive
topics.brief: Verbs + -ing vs + to; verbs that change meaning (remember/forget/stop/try/regret/mean/go on); adjectives + to; prepositions + -ing; make/let + bare infinitive.

topics.title: Contrast and concession
topics.brief: although/even though/though; despite/in spite of (+ -ing/the fact that); whereas/while; however/nevertheless/on the other hand; position and punctuation.

topics.title: Purpose, reason and result
topics.brief: so that/in order to/so as to/to; because of/due to/owing to/as/since; so…that/such…that; too/enough; as a result/therefore/consequently.

topics.title: Comparison
topics.brief: Comparatives and superlatives (regular and irregular); modifiers (far/much/a lot/slightly/by far/easily); as…as / not as…as / twice as…as; the + comparative, the + comparative; like vs as.

topics.title: Articles and quantifiers
topics.brief: a/an/the/zero article with general, specific and abstract nouns; countable/uncountable; few/a few/little/a little; plenty of/hardly any; all/both/neither/either/each/every/none of.

topics.title: Adjectives and adverbs
topics.brief: Order of adjectives; -ed vs -ing; gradable and ungradable adjectives with intensifiers (very/absolutely/really); adverb position (frequency, manner, sentence adverbs); adjectives vs adverbs (hard/hardly, late/lately).

topics.title: Emphasis: cleft sentences and basic inversion
topics.brief: What I need is…; It was Sofia who…; The reason (why)…is; Not only…but also; Never/Rarely + inversion (introductory); so/neither/nor do I.

topics.title: Questions: indirect, tags and echo
topics.brief: Indirect questions (Could you tell me where…); question tags with all auxiliaries, imperatives (will you?), let's (shall we?); negative questions; echo questions and short answers.

topics.title: Word formation for Use of English Part 3
topics.brief: Noun/verb/adjective/adverb families; negative prefixes (un/in/im/il/ir/dis/mis); suffixes (-ness/-ment/-tion/-ity/-ful/-less/-able/-ive/-ly); compound adjectives; plural or negative? — reading the sentence for the right form.

topics.title: The perfect aspect across tenses
topics.brief: Present, past and future perfect, simple and continuous; by/by the time/before; perfect infinitive and perfect -ing; subtle differences (has lived vs has been living).

topics.title: Advanced narrative and the future in the past
topics.brief: Past perfect continuous; was going to / would / was to (have) for plans that changed; would for past habits vs refusal; historic present for drama.

topics.title: Advanced ways of talking about the future
topics.brief: be to / be about to / be due to / be bound to / be on the verge of; future continuous for politeness and assumptions; future perfect continuous; will for assumptions and habits; shall in formal contexts.

topics.title: Unreal past and hypothetical meaning
topics.brief: as if/as though (+ past/past perfect); would rather/sooner (+ past for other subjects); it's (high/about) time; suppose/supposing/what if; wish + would for irritation; if only with all three times.

topics.title: Modal verbs: fine distinctions
topics.brief: needn't have vs didn't need to; may/might as well; could have (missed opportunity/annoyance); should/ought to have; will/would for habits and assumptions; dare and need as modals; be supposed to.

topics.title: Speculating about the past
topics.brief: must/can't/couldn't/may/might + have + participle; continuous forms (must have been waiting); was/were to have; ought to have; hedged speculation in formal writing.

topics.title: Advanced conditionals
topics.brief: Inverted conditionals (Had I known / Should you require / Were it not for); but for / if it weren't for; if + were to / if + should; provided that / on condition that / whether or not / assuming that; implied conditions (otherwise, or else).

topics.title: Inversion after negative and limiting adverbials
topics.brief: never/rarely/seldom/little/nowhere; not until/not only/no sooner…than/hardly…when/scarcely; only then/only when/only by; under no circumstances/on no account/in no way; so + adjective…that / such…that; inversion after as and than.

topics.title: Cleft sentences
topics.brief: it-clefts (It was the message that mattered), wh-clefts (What matters is…), all/the only thing…, the reason/place/person…, reversed wh-clefts (That's what I meant); clefts for contrast and correction.

topics.title: Emphasis and fronting
topics.brief: Emphatic do/does/did; fronting objects and adverbials (This I can accept); intensifying adverbs (utterly, downright, thoroughly) and collocation; own and very; the thing is; emphatic whatever/whoever.

topics.title: Advanced passive structures
topics.brief: Impersonal passive (it is believed that / she is believed to have); get-passive; passive infinitives and gerunds (to be told / being told); need + -ing; have/get something done vs have something happen; passive with phrasal verbs.

topics.title: Reporting: verbs, patterns and distance
topics.brief: Reporting verbs with their patterns (deny/insist/urge/object to/threaten/accuse of/blame for/dissuade from); reporting with hedges (claim/allege/is said to/is thought to); reported questions and requests; reporting without backshift; summarising what was said.

topics.title: Advanced verb patterns
topics.brief: Verbs + object + infinitive/-ing (I saw him leave / leaving); perfect and continuous infinitives (seems to have been); passive infinitives; verb + preposition + -ing; can't help/bear/stand; to vs to + -ing after object to/look forward to/be used to.

topics.title: Participle clauses
topics.brief: Present, past and perfect participle clauses (Having finished…, Built in 1900…); reduced relatives; with + noun + participle; participles after conjunctions (when asked, if given); avoiding dangling participles.

topics.title: Advanced relative clauses
topics.brief: Preposition + whom/which; whereby/wherein; whatever/whichever/whoever; of which/whose with things; all of whom / some of which; non-finite relatives (the first person to…); which for whole clauses in formal writing.

topics.title: Nominalisation and academic style
topics.brief: Turning verbs and adjectives into nouns (fail → failure, likely → likelihood); noun phrases with pre- and post-modification; abstract nouns with the + noun + of; impersonal subjects; when NOT to nominalise.

topics.title: Hedging and impersonal structures
topics.brief: it seems/appears/would seem that; tend to; arguably/presumably/apparently; there is some evidence that; modals for tentativeness (may/might/could); one; passive to avoid naming the agent; softeners in speech (sort of, I'd say).

topics.title: Discourse markers and cohesion
topics.brief: Formal linkers (albeit, notwithstanding, hence, thereby, whereby, in that); sequencing and referencing (the former/the latter, the above, such); spoken markers (mind you, as I was saying, anyway, that said); cohesion through repetition and synonyms.

topics.title: Substitution and ellipsis
topics.brief: so/not after think/hope/suppose; do so/did so; one/ones; ellipsis after auxiliaries and to (I'd like to); if so / if not; omitting repeated subjects and verbs; the same; leaving out that and relative pronouns.

topics.title: Concession and contrast at C1
topics.brief: much as / however + adjective / no matter how / whatever; whilst; albeit; even so / all the same / that said; granted / admittedly; for all + noun; may…but; as in Tired as he was.

topics.title: Advanced comparison
topics.brief: the + comparative, the + comparative with ellipsis; nowhere near / nothing like / by far / every bit as / just as; not so much X as Y; comparatives with clauses (than had been expected); like vs as vs as if; as … as any; all the more.

topics.title: Articles and determiners at C1
topics.brief: Generic the (the tiger, the rich); zero article with abstract and institutional nouns (in hospital, at university); the with superlatives, ordinals and unique things; quite a / rather a / such a; half/all/both (of); a with jobs and units of measure; determiner + own.

topics.title: Word formation at C1
topics.brief: Nominalising suffixes (-ance/-ence/-ity/-ism/-hood); negative prefixes and their nuances (dis-/mis-/un-/in-/non-); compound adjectives (well-established, time-consuming); conversion (to google); -en/-ify/-ise verbs; strategy for Use of English Part 3.

topics.title: Phrasal verbs, dependent prepositions and idioms
topics.brief: Phrasal verbs with several meanings; what particles mean (up = completion, out = disappearance, off = separation, through = completion); separable/inseparable; dependent prepositions (Use of English Part 2); idiomatic collocations for C1 speaking and writing.

topics.title: The verb be: am, is, are
topics.brief: I am / you are / he is…; contractions (I'm, she's, they're); negatives (isn't, aren't); questions and short answers (Are you…? Yes, I am.); age, nationality, feelings and jobs with be; the classic trap I have 12 years.

topics.title: Nouns: a/an, plurals, this/that/these/those
topics.brief: a/an with a consonant or vowel sound (a dog, an apple, a uniform); plural -s/-es/-ies and the irregulars (children, people, feet, teeth, mice); this/that/these/those with near and far; What's this? / What are those?

topics.title: have got: what you have
topics.brief: I have got / she has got; contractions ('ve got, 's got); negatives (haven't got, hasn't got); questions (Have you got…? Has she got…?) and short answers; family, pets, possessions and describing people (She's got long hair).

topics.title: my, your, his, her and 's
topics.brief: Possessive adjectives (my, your, his, her, its, our, their); the apostrophe s (Sofia's bag, my parents' car); Whose…?; his vs her vs its; object pronouns (me, him, her, us, them) after verbs and prepositions.

topics.title: Present simple: I, you, we, they
topics.brief: Routines, likes and facts with I/you/we/they; negatives with don't; questions with Do…? and short answers (Yes, I do. / No, they don't.); like/love/hate + noun; everyday time words (every day, at the weekend).

topics.title: Present simple: he, she, it and the -s
topics.brief: The third-person -s (she plays, he goes, it has); spelling -s/-es/-ies (watches, goes, studies); negatives with doesn't + base verb; questions with Does…?; the number one A1 error: She play / She don't.

topics.title: How often? always, usually, sometimes, never
topics.brief: Adverbs of frequency and their place (after be, before other verbs); once/twice a week, every day, on Mondays; at/on/in with times, days and months; How often do you…?; a day in the life of the cast.

topics.title: Question words: What, Where, When, Who, How
topics.brief: What/Where/When/Who/Why/How/Which/How many/How old/How much; question word + be or do/does; word order in questions; the questions of Speaking Part 1 (Where are you from? What do you like doing?); answering in full.

topics.title: there is / there are and where things are
topics.brief: there is / there are with a, an, some and any; negatives and questions (Is there…? Are there any…?); prepositions of place (in, on, under, next to, behind, in front of, between, opposite, near); describing a room, a town, a picture (Listening Part 1).

topics.title: can and can't
topics.brief: can/can't for ability (I can swim), possibility and permission; questions (Can you…?) and short answers; can + base verb (never can to); Can I…? for asking, Can you…? for requests; pronunciation of can vs can't.

topics.title: Present continuous: what is happening now
topics.brief: am/is/are + -ing for now and today; spelling of -ing (sitting, making, studying); negatives and questions (Is she sleeping?); look! / listen! / now / at the moment; describing a picture of the cast; first contrast with the present simple.

topics.title: Imperatives and Let's
topics.brief: Instructions and classroom language (Open your books. Don't run.); negative imperatives with Don't; Let's + verb for suggestions; please and polite orders; signs and notices (Reading Part 1); recipes, directions and rules.

topics.title: Present simple: be, have got and routines
topics.brief: am/is/are and have got; routines and facts; third person -s/-es; adverbs of frequency and their position; negatives and questions with do/does; short answers.

topics.title: Present continuous
topics.brief: am/is/are + -ing for now and around now; spelling of -ing (sit → sitting, make → making); simple vs continuous with now/today vs every day; state verbs (like, want, know, understand) stay simple.

topics.title: Past simple
topics.brief: was/were; regular -ed (spelling: stop → stopped, study → studied) and the most useful irregular verbs; negatives and questions with did; ago, last, yesterday, in 2019.

topics.title: Past continuous with when and while
topics.brief: was/were + -ing for a background action; past simple for the event that interrupts; when vs while; the two orders of the sentence.

topics.title: Present perfect: ever, never, just, already, yet
topics.brief: have/has + past participle; regular and irregular participles; ever/never in questions and negatives; just/already/yet and where they go; been vs gone.

topics.title: Present perfect or past simple?
topics.brief: Finished time (yesterday, last week, in 2020, ago) → past simple; unfinished time or no time (ever, this week, for, since) → present perfect; for vs since; How long…?

topics.title: Talking about the future
topics.brief: will for decisions, offers and predictions; going to for plans and things you can see coming; present continuous for arrangements with a time; shall I / shall we for offers and suggestions.

topics.title: can, could, may: ability, requests and permission
topics.brief: can/can't for ability and permission; could for past ability and polite requests; may for polite permission; be able to; Can I…? / Could you…? / May I…? and their answers.

topics.title: must, have to, should: rules and advice
topics.brief: must and have to for rules; mustn't vs don't have to (the big difference); should/shouldn't for advice; need to; had to for past obligation; the language of signs and notices (Reading Part 1).

topics.title: Zero and first conditional
topics.brief: if/when + present simple for things that are always true; if + present, will/won't for real future situations; imperatives and can in the result; unless = if not; the comma when if comes first.

topics.title: Questions and short answers
topics.brief: Question words (what/where/when/who/why/how/which/whose); how + adjective (how often/how long/how much/how many/how far); word order with be, do/does/did and modals; short answers; questions about the subject (Who called?).

topics.title: Linking words: and, but, or, so, because
topics.brief: and/but/or/so/because; then/after that/when/before/after/while for time; also/too/as well; that's why; joining two short sentences into one for Writing Parts 6 and 7.

topics.title: Verb patterns: like doing, want to do
topics.brief: like/love/hate/enjoy/don't mind + -ing; want/need/would like/hope/decide/learn + to; go + -ing (go swimming); let's/why don't we/how about + -ing; start/begin with both.

topics.title: who, which, that, where
topics.brief: Defining relative clauses to say which person, thing or place you mean; who for people, which/that for things, where for places; leaving out the relative pronoun when it is the object (the film I saw).

topics.title: there is/are and have got
topics.brief: there is/there are with some/any/a/an; there was/were; have got vs has got and their questions; have got vs there is (my town has got vs there is in my town); a lot of/lots of.

topics.title: Imperatives, suggestions and offers
topics.brief: Imperatives and negative imperatives (Don't forget…) for instructions, notices and messages; Let's…, Shall we…?, Why don't we…?, How about + -ing?, Would you like…?; accepting and refusing politely.

topics.title: Telling a story: sequencing and past tenses together
topics.brief: First/then/next/after that/finally; one day/suddenly/in the end; past simple and past continuous in the same story; time expressions; the shape of a 35-word story for Writing Part 7.

topics.title: Comparatives and superlatives
topics.brief: -er/-est and more/most; spelling (big → bigger, happy → happiest); irregular (good/bad/far); than; the with superlatives; as…as and not as…as; much/a lot + comparative.

topics.title: Adjectives and adverbs
topics.brief: Adjectives before nouns and after be/look/feel; -ed vs -ing (bored/boring); adverbs of manner with -ly (and irregular: well, fast, hard); too + adjective, adjective + enough, very/really/quite; two adjectives in order (a big red bag).

topics.title: a, an, the or nothing?
topics.brief: a/an for one of many and for jobs; the for something known or unique; no article with meals, sports, languages and plural general nouns; go to school/bed/work; at home; the cinema/the beach/the station.

topics.title: Countable and uncountable: some, any, much, many
topics.brief: Countable vs uncountable nouns (money, information, homework, food); some/any in statements, questions and offers; much/many/a lot of; a few/a little; How much…? / How many…?; a piece of, a bottle of.

topics.title: Prepositions of time and place
topics.brief: at/in/on for time (at 6, on Monday, in May) and place (at school, in the kitchen, on the wall); from…to, until, by, during, for; next to, opposite, between, behind, in front of, near; prepositions after verbs (listen to, wait for, look at).

topics.title: Pronouns and possessives
topics.brief: Subject and object pronouns; possessive adjectives (my) vs possessive pronouns (mine); the apostrophe s; whose; one/ones; reflexive pronouns (myself) and each other; someone/anything/everywhere.

topics.title: Word building and spelling
topics.brief: Nouns from verbs (swim → swimmer, teach → teacher); -ly adverbs; un- for opposites (happy → unhappy); compound nouns (bus stop, football match); plural spelling (-s/-es/-ies); the words that always cause spelling mistakes in Listening Part 2 and Writing.

topics.title: Present simple and continuous
topics.brief: Routines, facts and timetables vs actions now and temporary situations; state verbs; present continuous for future arrangements; adverbs of frequency; always + -ing for habits that annoy.

topics.title: Past simple and past continuous
topics.brief: Past simple for finished events; past continuous for background and interrupted actions; when/while/as; time expressions; the irregular verbs you must know at B1.

topics.title: Past perfect
topics.brief: had + past participle for the earlier of two past events; after/before/by the time/when; past perfect with already/just/never; the story order vs the sentence order.

topics.title: Present perfect simple and continuous
topics.brief: for/since/ever/never/just/already/yet/still; been vs gone; How long…?; present perfect vs past simple; present perfect continuous for how long something has been happening.

topics.title: Future forms
topics.brief: will/won't for predictions, decisions and promises; going to for plans and evidence; present continuous for arrangements; present simple for timetables; future time clauses (when/as soon as/until/before + present simple).

topics.title: used to and would for past habits
topics.brief: used to/didn't use to/Did you use to…? for past habits and states that are different now; would for repeated past actions (not states); used to vs be used to (intro).

topics.title: Obligation and advice: must, have to, should, ought to
topics.brief: must vs have to; mustn't vs don't have to/needn't; should/ought to/had better for advice; had to/didn't have to in the past; be allowed to; notices and rules (Reading Part 1).

topics.title: Deduction: must, might, may, could, can't
topics.brief: Present deduction (must be/can't be/might be) and past deduction (must have/can't have/might have + participle); degrees of certainty; deduction must vs obligation must.

topics.title: Ability, possibility, requests and offers
topics.brief: can/could/be able to/managed to for ability; may/might/could for possibility; Could you…?/Would you mind…? for requests; Shall I…?/I'll… for offers; may/can for permission.

topics.title: First and second conditional
topics.brief: if + present, will for real futures; if + past, would for unreal or unlikely situations; unless/as long as/in case; if I were you; will vs would in the result; mixing them up is the classic B1 error.

topics.title: Third conditional
topics.brief: if + past perfect, would have + participle for imaginary past situations and regrets; could have/might have in the result; contractions (I'd have); the difference from the second conditional.

topics.title: wish, hope, I'd rather, I'd prefer
topics.brief: wish + past simple for the present, wish + past perfect for the past, wish + would for annoying things; hope + present/will; I'd rather + verb, I'd prefer + to; if only (intro).

topics.title: The passive: present and past
topics.brief: be + past participle in present simple, past simple and present perfect; by + agent (and when to leave it out); questions and negatives; why writers choose the passive (processes, news, formal notices).

topics.title: The passive in other tenses and with modals
topics.brief: Present and past continuous passive (is being built, was being repaired); past perfect passive; future passive (will be sent); modal passive (must be worn, can be seen); have something done (intro).

topics.title: Reported speech: statements
topics.brief: say vs tell; tense changes (present → past, will → would, can → could, past → past perfect); pronoun, time and place changes (tomorrow → the next day); when the tense does not change.

topics.title: Reported questions, commands and requests
topics.brief: Reported yes/no questions with if/whether; wh- questions and their word order; ask/tell/want sb (not) to; suggest/advise/warn/promise/offer/refuse and their patterns.

topics.title: Relative clauses
topics.brief: Defining clauses with who/which/that/where/whose/when; leaving out the pronoun when it is the object; non-defining clauses with commas (intro); that is not used after a comma.

topics.title: Verb patterns: -ing or to?
topics.brief: Verbs + -ing (enjoy, finish, avoid, mind, suggest); verbs + to (want, decide, hope, promise, learn); both with a change of meaning (remember/forget/stop/try); make/let + verb; prepositions + -ing; adjectives + to.

topics.title: Linking: contrast, reason, purpose and result
topics.brief: although/though/even though/however/despite/in spite of; because/because of/as/since; so that/in order to/to; so/therefore/as a result; too/enough; punctuation with linkers in Writing Parts 1 and 2.

topics.title: Question tags, indirect questions and so/neither
topics.brief: Question tags with be, do, modals and have; intonation and answers; indirect questions (Could you tell me where…? Do you know if…?) with no inversion; So do I / Neither can I; short replies.

topics.title: Comparison at B1
topics.brief: Comparatives and superlatives, regular, irregular and with more/most; modifiers (much/far/a bit/a little/slightly); as…as/not as…as; the…the…; less/the least; comparative adverbs (more quickly, better); too/enough.

topics.title: Articles and quantifiers
topics.brief: a/an/the/zero article with places, meals, institutions and general nouns; all/most/some/no/none of; both/either/neither; each/every; too much/too many/enough/plenty of; a few/few/a little/little.

topics.title: Adjectives and adverbs
topics.brief: Order of adjectives (a lovely old wooden box); -ed vs -ing; adverbs of manner, degree and frequency and their position; adjectives vs adverbs (hard/hardly, late/lately, good/well); so/such; extreme adjectives with absolutely.

topics.title: Word formation: prefixes, suffixes and families
topics.brief: Word families (succeed/success/successful/successfully); noun suffixes (-tion/-ment/-ness/-er/-ist); adjective suffixes (-ful/-less/-able/-ive/-ous); -ly adverbs; negative prefixes (un-/dis-/im-/in-/ir-); re-/over-/under-; spelling changes; how Reading Parts 5 and 6 test them.
